newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ADVERTISERS OUT OF STEP WITH NEW S.AFRICA - NAIDOO.
newsitem.headline: ADVERTISERS OUT OF STEP WITH NEW S.AFRICA - NAIDOO.

text.p: South Africa's minister in charge of broadcasting accused advertisers on Wednesday of deserting state television because it was showing too many black faces.

Posts, Telecommunications and Broadcasting Minister Jay Naidoo told parliament the South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC) expected a deficit in the year ending September 30 of 21 million rand ($4.6 million).
"The main reasons that they have given so far have been the decrease in the licence fees and advertising revenue," he said.
SABC has struggled to persuade viewers to pay TV licence fees and has suffered a drop in advertising since revising its programming earlier this year.
"Some people are very unhappy with seeing so many black faces on TV and are now withdrawing their advertising ... people need to get used to the reality of the new South Africa," Naidoo said.
One of the effects of SABC's new programming has been to reduce the amount of Afrikaans-language content.
